paragraphs.text: 1 The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi. 2 "I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, 3 And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the wolves of the wilderness. 4 Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever. 5 And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say, The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel.
The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: [1]

Some translate the word "oracle" here as "burden." For Israel in its wickedness, the word of the Lord did not represent joy, gladness and sweetness, because it uncovered their wounds without flattery. Therefore they counted it a burden upon them, which grieved them so that they were unable to hear it. It is a burden to the one who does not seek the salvation of his soul, but those who are earnest about the salvation of their souls find it an easy and sweet yoke (Mt 11:30).
I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?
Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD, yet I loved Jacob [2].

Since this book reveals the calling of all the nations and peoples to accept the faith, it begins by affirming God's love for His people, freely and without any merit on their part. Yet they made light of His love, despised His name and defiled the offerings and sacrifices. For this reason God no longer took pleasure in them as long as they walked in this way, and He opens the door to all the nations, from the rising of the sun to its going down, that His name may be glorified in all the earth.

He began to open the wounds of His people in order to cleanse and treat them, assuring them that He does this not out of hatred or enmity but out of love and tenderness. For this reason God's message to them begins with the words: "I have loved you." This is what God has affirmed continually through His prophets: "Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee" (Jer 31:3). "When Israel was a child, then I loved him" (Hos 11:1), "for the LORD delighteth in thee" (Isa 62:4).

Thus He begins His speech by declaring His love, to affirm that if He rebukes, it is because He is a Father: "As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten" (Rev 3:19). He rebukes them because they did not return love for love.

Man needs someone who loves him and who receives his love. That is why God so often assures His children: "I have loved you." But when circumstances that seem harsh and bitter in his eyes pass over a man, he asks within himself: "Where is God's love for me?"
They doubted His love for them and made light of it: "Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?" By saying this they belittle God's love and His care for them.

"Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD, yet I loved Jacob" [2]. The Jews often think that God is bound to love them because they are the sons of Abraham, and that He repays them with love as one who is in debt to their father. Therefore He says to them: if I loved you in return for Abraham's love for Me, then Esau should have enjoyed My love more than Jacob, for he was the firstborn; yet Jacob seized the love of God by practical faith, while Esau fell under wrath by the hardness of his heart. God's love is not based on partiality, nor on mere bodily kinship, for Esau and Jacob were twin brothers in one womb, and Jacob enjoyed entering into a covenant with God, while Esau deprived himself of the gift.
This gift that Jacob received was free; he had no merit in it. It is according to God's good pleasure, but not by compulsion or force; rather it comes through man's response to the free divine grace.
* God foreknows sinful people while they are yet in their mothers' wombs (Gen 25:23).

* "The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies" (Ps 58:3)... What is this? Let us examine it more attentively, for perhaps he says this because God foreknew the men who are sinners while they were in their mothers' wombs. Therefore, when Rebecca was still with child, having conceived twins, it was said: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2; Rom 9:13). For it was said: "The elder shall serve the younger." God's judgment was hidden at that time, but from the womb, from the very origin, sinners go astray. From what do they go astray? From the truth. From what do they go astray? From the blessed city, from the blessed life.

St. Augustine * Cain despised his brother, as he despised God. How did he despise Him? By his impudent answer to God: "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Gen 4:9). Esau despised his brother, and he too despised God. Therefore God said: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Rom 9:13; Mal 1:2-3).

St. John Chrysostom * We think rightly when we say that "God loves justice and hates robbery by injustice." This does not mean that He has a leaning toward the one or the other, and accepts what is opposed, to the point of preferring this and not preferring that. For that is the characteristic of creatures. Rather it means that, as a judge, He loves the righteous and helps them, and turns away from the wicked.

St. Athanasius the Apostolic God declared His love for Israel, saying: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt" (Hos 11:1), for He called him a child and His son. Without partiality, when the people of Israel persisted in their evils, His prophet St. John the Baptist calls them: "O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?" (Mt 3:7). Thus there is no partiality with God!

* It is the fruit of their folly and their childish thinking that they suffer this punishment. I called them out of Egypt and freed them from harsh bondage, but they showed ingratitude to Me and chose the worship of idols. I who taught them to walk, and healed them of their hideous conduct, and showed them fatherly tenderness, and used every kind of remedy with them, they refused to know Me, although I had preserved them from a double destruction at the hands of the invaders. They are like those who have fastened their nails into Me, and I love them as though that were a chain.

Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * Israel was called a son symbolically from the time he was in Egypt (Mt 2:15), but he lost his sonship by worshipping Baal and offering incense to idols, so John gave them a name fitting them, "generation of vipers" (Mt 3:7). Since they lost the title of sonship that was poured out upon them through grace in the days of Moses, they received from John a name that matched their deeds.
St. Ephrem the Syrian And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains waste, and his heritage for the wolves of the wilderness? [3]

Edom (Esau) defied the God of Israel and cared nothing for His divine will, so in due time he fell into everlasting ruin. Israel, on the other hand, who was under chastening, received the blessing of the revelation of God's glory within his borders. This work goes on continually in the spiritual realm. If a Jew or a Gentile defies the God of hosts, he becomes like a spiritual Edom; God is long-suffering toward him, and when his cup is filled with evil he falls into eternal destruction. Meanwhile many of the Gentiles who were the stubborn spiritual Edom, when they return to the Lord, become the new Israel, filled with divine glories.

Esau was violent with his brother, his father and his mother, so he married two daughters of Heth, "which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah" (Gen 26:35). He drank of the cup that he had filled for his parents and his brother, so ruin befell his heart, and this ruin turned back even upon the mountains of Seir, which were "his heritage." The army of the Chaldeans came and laid them waste until they became a dwelling for the wolves of the wilderness, having become utterly desolate.
The sons of Esau, or the sons of Edom, who rejoiced at the destruction of Jerusalem (Ps 137:7), drank from the very cup of staggering that they had filled for others.

God was very long-suffering toward Edom and left it generation after generation, so that some thought that God's threats against them were only words without action. But at last it fell into perpetual ruin, and there has been no kingdom of Edom since.

* Rebecca carried the two, Jacob and Esau. The seed is one, but the two who were conceived are different. The womb is one, and the two she carried are different. Did not the free woman conceive Esau? They struggled together within their mother's womb, there they quarreled, and it was said to Rebecca: "Two nations are in thy womb"; two men, two nations, yet they struggled in the womb. How many wicked people there are in the Church! One womb conceives them until they are separated in the end, and the wicked cry out against the good, and both struggle in the bowels of their one mother.

* Who is so foolish and wicked as to say that God is unable to change the evil will of men, however He wishes, whenever He wishes and wherever He wishes, and make it good? But when He works, He works through mercy; and when He does not work, it is through justice. For "he hath mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth" (Rom 9:18). Now when the Apostle said this, he was praising grace, which he spoke of when he connected it with the twins in Rebecca's womb. "For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth; it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger" (Rom 9:11-12). Consequently he points to another prophetic testimony, where it is written: "Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2-3). And since he realized how what he had said might cause disturbance to those whose understanding could not enter into this depth of grace, he added: "What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid" (Rom 9:14). And yet it seems that, unjustly, without any merit from good or evil works, God loves one and hates the other. Now if the Apostle had wished us to understand that there were future good works of the one, which God had doubtless foreknown, he would not have said: "Not of works" (Rom 9:11), but he would have said: "from future works." Thus he wished to resolve the difficulty; or rather, he wished not to leave a difficulty to be resolved. For he added at once: "God forbid" (to show that there is no unrighteousness in God). "For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion" (Rom 9:15). Now who but a fool thinks there is unrighteousness in God, whether when He inflicts a penalty on one who deserves it, or shows mercy to one who does not deserve it? Finally the Apostle concludes by saying: "So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy" (Rom 9:16).

St. Augustine * From the beginning of the world, of the two sons born to Adam, Abel the younger was chosen, while Cain the elder, being a type of the unbelieving Jews, was condemned. Afterward, in the time of Abraham, the same type was fulfilled in Sarah and Hagar. Sarah was barren for a long time as a type of the Church, while Hagar, as a type of the Jewish synagogue, conceived a son at once. Here the younger son, Isaac, was received into the inheritance, while Ishmael the elder was deprived of it. This truth appears to be fulfilled in the two: Jacob the younger was loved by God, while Esau was rejected, as it is written: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2-3). This type is also known to be fulfilled in the two sisters whom Jacob took as wives: Rachel the younger, whom Jacob loved more than Leah the elder. In fact, from the former was born Joseph, who was sold into Egypt as a type of our Lord and Savior. So Leah was weak of sight, while Rachel was beautiful in form; this too has a meaning: Leah is understood as the synagogue of the Jews, and Rachel points to the Church. A man whose bodily eyes are inflamed cannot look upon the brightness of the sun. So the synagogue, whose heart's eyes were filled with envy and malice against our Lord and Savior, as with a flood filled with poison, cannot look upon the loftiness of Christ, who is the Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2).
Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.
Thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down.
And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever. [4]

Edom thought that it was able by itself to rise from this ruin that had come upon it, without reforming the heart and driving out the wolves within. Edom fell into vain hopes, and they thought they could rebuild the desolate places, as happened with Jerusalem.

By saying "we will return and build the desolate places," they see that the matter is in their own hands and depends on their military capabilities and their planning, whether God wills it or not. Therefore "thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down." For they cannot stand in defiance before God.

By their defiance they become an example and a warning to souls that exalt themselves against God. "And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever" [4]. All understand the words of Job: "Who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?" (Job 9:4).

When the Jews rejected the Lord Christ and opposed His Gospel and His Church, they became Edomites, and this saying was fulfilled in them, for when they tried to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem in the days of the Emperor Hadrian, God demolished what they had built, by an earthquake and the bursting forth of tongues of fire, so that they were forced to stop building.
* If God uttered a thousand words accusing us, we would not be able to answer a single one. What does the prophet say? "In thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Ps 143:2).

St. John Chrysostom * "I acknowledge my sin to You, my God, and You have lifted away the iniquity of my heart" (cf. Ps 32:5). I do not dispute with You the judgment, O Truth, for I do not wish to deceive myself, lest my iniquity stand against me.
St. Augustine And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say:
The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel. [5]

Since the heart of Edom became a wasteland, with no trace of love in it, but bearing the malice of wolves, its mountains turned to ruin and its heritage became the property of the wolves of the wilderness. Now that Israel, under chastening, asks for divine intervention, God is glorified in his borders as He is glorified in his inner depths. This is God's good pleasure, that the whole world become the new, spiritual Israel, bearing the glory of God within and without.

The Word of God came to transfer us, through Baptism, from sonship to the enemy of good to sonship to God, and to change us from the Edom that bears the barren, wolfish heart into the new Israel that bears the divine glory.
A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master.
If then I be a father, where is mine honour?
And if I be a master, where is my fear?
Saith the LORD of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name.
And ye say, Wherein have we despised thy name? [6]

By the law of nature a son honors his father, and by the laws of the world a servant fears his master, obeys his commands and is careful to serve his interests. The son who does not honor his father falls under the curse of natural law, and the servant who does not listen to his master falls under the penalty of the laws of society. This is the position of the son and the servant; so what is the position of the priest, who is governed by the divine law? Which has the greater claim to obedience, the divine law or the laws of nature and society?

If the priest desires to be called a father (Judg 18:19), and if some look to him as a leader whom they must obey, then the priest must deal with God as a son and a servant of His. For how can the priest call the people to honor God as a Father, and to submit to Him as a Master, when he does not bear the same spirit? St. Paul says: "Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?" (Heb 12:9).

* God asks of all creatures: "If then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). If human life has no master to oversee it, it turns into a chaos that calls for lamentation. This is what became of the heavenly powers that rebelled and stiffened their necks against God the Almighty, refusing to submit to Him, not because they were of an uncreated nature, but because the cause of their disobedience was rebellion against the Creator.

* It is said: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master" (Mal 1:6). Of these two, servitude is offered by the creature, and the other, which may be called intimate friendship, is accomplished by the Holy Spirit.

St. Basil the Great * Our prayer must agree with the "good" will of the One to whom we pray, by glorifying Him in the opening of the prayer. That is why we were commanded to begin with nothing but the words "Our Father which art in heaven."

Indeed many words concerning the glorification of God are spread through the pages of the Holy Scripture, but we never found a commandment for the people of the Jews to say "Our Father," that is, they did not pray to Him as sons but as servants, as those who still lived according to the flesh.
I say that they did not take God as their Father, though they could have done so had they not disobeyed the Law they were commanded to keep. Therefore the following texts came:
"I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2).
"I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High" (Ps 82:6).
"If then I be a father, where is mine honour... etc." (Mal 1:6)

These texts show that they were not accepted as sons of God, and they are also a prophecy of what Christians would be, who take God as their Father, as the Evangelist says: "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God" (Jn 1:12). And as the Apostle Paul says: "The heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant" (Gal 4:1), pointing to the spirit of adoption which we have received, by which we cry, "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15).

St. Augustine * The glory of fathers is the holiness of their sons, and the honor of masters is the fear of their servants, while the opposite brings insult and confusion. For He says: "Because of you My name is blasphemed among the Gentiles."

The Didascalia * "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2)... He does not point to their fellowship with all mankind in expressions of the loftiness of their birth, but rather to a surpassing help in that they became His sons. God takes the initiative in every matter by giving gifts. In the creation of man He began by honoring him even before He brought him into being, saying: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Gen 1:26)... Here one can see that God honors the adoption of man.

* Those who have become sons and enjoy the spiritual food have the right to glorify their Father. The Scripture says: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master." You have become His son and you enjoy the spiritual food; you receive His Body and Blood, which give you a new birth. Therefore, repay such a kindness by glorifying the One who gave it to you. And when you read these words, make sure of your attachment to them. When he says: "I will extol thee, my God, O king" (Ps 145:1), give testimony of your intimate relationship, so that God may say of you, as of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob" (Ex 3:6). I mean, if you say, "My God, my King," and not only say this but also give testimony of such love, He in turn says the same thing about you: "My servant, My companion," which He said also of Moses.
* He who has the fear is not meddlesome, but falls down and worships. He who has the fear does not raise questions out of curiosity, but on the contrary offers praise and glory.

St. John Chrysostom * Last week I spoke at sufficient length for the correction of those who do not give thanks to the Creator for the divine gifts they enjoy, those who, while benefiting from heavenly tenderness, as ungrateful and unworthy people do not know the giver of the tenderness. They are ungrateful, I say, those who do not fear God as servants toward their master, nor honor Him as sons toward their father. God says through the prophet: "If I be a master, where is my fear? and if I be a father, where is mine honour?" (Mal 1:6), meaning: if you are a servant, offer service to the Master with fear, and if you are a son, show your father reverent love. But since you do not give thanks, you neither love God nor fear Him. You are an arrogant servant or a proud son. The good Christian must praise his Father and Master continually, and practice all good works for His glory. This is as the Apostle says: "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Cor 10:33).

Maximus, bishop of Turin * Concerning God, who is one alone, bearing a person with two aspects as Father and Master, we are bound to love Him since we are His sons, and to fear Him since we are His servants.

Lactantius * This fear or love for which God rebukes us, each one according to what suits him, saying: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). For the servant must fear: "And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes" (Lk 12:47).

* There is a twofold fear: 1. One is for beginners, that is, those who are still under the terrifying bondage, of which we read: "a servant his master" (Mal 1:6). And in the Gospel He says: "Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth" (Jn 15:15). "And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever" (Jn 8:35). Therefore God teaches us to pass from the fear of punishment to the fullness of the freedom of love and the confidence of the beloved sons of God. Finally, the blessed Apostle, by the power of God's love, passed through the stage of the bondage of fear, so that he might despise earthly things and declare that he had been enriched with the good things of God, when he says: "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2 Tim 1:7). To those too who are kindled with perfect love toward their heavenly Father, and who through divine adoption have become sons and not servants, the Apostle says: "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15). 2. As for the other fear, the prophet speaks of the sevenfold Spirit, who according to the mystery of the Incarnation rests in fullness upon the incarnate God: "And the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD" (Isa 11:2). And he adds in particular: "And his delight shall be in the fear of the LORD" (Isa 11:3). We notice that he did not go on to say, "the spirit of fear shall rest upon You," but "his delight shall be in the fear of the LORD." For this is the greatness and the wealth of this fear, that when it settles upon someone with its power it does not take possession of a part of his mind but of all his mind. And this is not without understanding, for it is closely bound to love, which "never faileth."
Father Chaeremon A grave accusation is directed at the people as well as the priests, and a grave answer: "Wherein have we despised thy name?" It brings us before a sad and terrifying picture.

The gravest thing in the matter is the spiritual blindness that struck them all, so that they did not feel that they were despising God's name; perhaps they even boasted that they offered offerings and sacrifices and practiced worship with exactness according to the Law.

The Jewish people prided themselves on having the tribe of Levi, from whom came the priests whom the Lord had chosen for Himself, who offered sacrifices and offerings that were pleasing to God. Now God Himself reveals to them that the priests who intercede for them to obtain blessings had lost the blessing, the holiness and God's good pleasure. Who then can lift up the face of the people before God?

God speaks through the prophet to call the priests to account. If they were appointed judges in the house of the Lord, it was so that they themselves might first practice the commandment and live it, or else fall under judgment.

* Be obedient to your bishop; obey him as your spiritual father. Sons love, and servants fear. He says: "If then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). In your case, one person may bear many labors for your honor, being at the same time a monk, a bishop and an uncle. But bishops must know that they are priests and not lords. Let them restore to the priesthood the honor that befits it.

St. Jerome * This is your duty, O bishop: not to ignore the sins of the people, and not to reject those who are repentant, lest you break the Lord's flock through lack of skill, or insult His new name which has been placed upon a people, while you yourself are rebuked as happened with the ancient shepherds of whom God said to Jeremiah: "Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot" (Jer 12:10). And in another passage: "My anger was kindled against the shepherds, and My wrath against the lambs" (cf. Zech 10:3). And in another place: "O priests, that despise my name" (Mal 1:6).
* It is clear that the bishops and priests who are thus called in vain do not escape God's judgment.
The Didascalia

7 Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar; and ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say, The table of the LORD is contemptible. 8 And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts. 9 And now, I pray you, beseech God that he will be gracious unto us: this hath been by your means: will he regard your persons? saith the LORD of hosts.
Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar.
And ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee?
In that ye say, The table of the LORD is contemptible. [7]

The accusation He directs against the priests is the despising of God's name and the defiling of His holy things. What is graver than this is that when they hear the accusation they answer: "Wherein have we despised thy name? Wherein have we polluted thee?" Such questions reveal either the priests' ignorance of the truth, which is a grave matter since they are blind leaders leading the people, or their knowledge of what they are doing, so that they answer with a measure of unseemly boldness, and this is worse! Their committing evil, whether knowingly or unknowingly, is extremely grave by reason of their position of leadership.

"The table of the LORD is contemptible": perhaps this means the table of the showbread or the altar of burnt offerings. It was called this because the priests and the people ate from it, as though God, who accepts the sacrifices, wished the priests and the people to share with Him as at a table of reconciliation.

By their sharing in the sacrifices offered to idols they despise the table of the Lord, since they wish for fellowship with God and the idols, or with God and Satan. By this they are counted as those who have polluted the table of the Lord [12].
They despised the table of the Lord by offering defective sacrifices, giving the first place to themselves and counting God unworthy to be offered the best of what they had.

They offered sacrifices on the table of the Lord, or the altar, and thought they were pleasing Him, not realizing that they were despising Him and polluting His altar. Therefore they ask: "Wherein have we polluted thee?" They offered sacrifices, but their hearts were far from the Lord, and opposed to Him, not accepting His commandment and not wishing to enjoy fellowship with Him.
And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil?
And if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil?
Offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts. [8]

They offered the sacrifices that were fit for no other purpose, reckoning that any burnt offering is burned with fire, so they grudged offering animals that were fit for sale or trade or any other purpose, as though they were offering God their leftovers. In the Book of Deuteronomy it says concerning sacrifices: "And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the LORD thy God. Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck, and as the hart" (Deut 15:21-22).

The sacrifice of the blind refers to practicing worship without spiritual benefit, so that we are like one who performs a duty in ignorance, without looking to God to learn His joyful heavenly mysteries.

The sacrifice of the lame refers to the person who does not enjoy the Lord Christ as the divine Way by which he goes forth toward the Father's bosom, so that his soul may be settled, rest and be comforted by the heavenly Father.

The sacrifice of the sick refers to the one who practices worship with indifference, without fixing his eyes on the Lord, the heavenly Physician, so that his sick soul stands still without seeking true healing.

It is to be noted in the three preceding sacrifices, whether that of the blind, the lame or the sick, that man practices his worship with the body and not the heart, with the letter and not the spirit, so that he carries a heart without enlightenment, without spiritual movement, and in slackness!

He reproaches them that what they practice in their relationship with Him they would not dare to do with a king or governor whose favor they seek, since they could not offer a gift or tribute with a lame animal or a crooked one.

* So was the offering of Cain the murderer rejected. God said to him: "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?" (Gen 4:7). So also were all the offerings of Israel rejected, so that they received the curse that the prophet spoke: "But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing" (Mal 1:14). He rebukes and reproves them, saying: "Offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or show thee tenderness? saith the LORD" (cf. Mal 1:8). How then can any speech directed to God during the service of prayer, showing any kind of disrespect, be acceptable to God, a speech full of every kind of distraction, that is, a sick speech hindered by many interruptions (through distraction of thought)? Such a kind would not be acceptable even if offered to the most insignificant human being if addressed to him in this way. A prayer offering full of disturbance and the service of a careless heart are like the sacrifice of a ram that is wholly defective.

Observe with us: if God takes no pleasure in sacrifice and offering (Ps 40:6), but seeks sacrifices of praise, thanksgiving and gratitude (Ps 51:16; 116:17; Jer 33:11), then He accepts them from pure, holy lips, but whoever offers them from unclean lips, which curse and do not bless, lie and do not speak the truth, judge and do not show mercy, his are counted unclean sacrifices. It is as though the man were offering the sacrifice of the blind, the lame or the sick.
And now, I pray you, beseech God that he will be gracious unto us.
This hath been by your means.
Will he regard your persons? saith the LORD of hosts. [9]

Some see that a plague came upon the land, when raids of locusts attacked the fields and ate what was green (Mal 3:11), and the priests cried out but the Lord did not answer because of their wickedness. Therefore He gives them the counsel to return to God in repentance and He will hear their prayers, for themselves as well as for the people. As the psalmist says: "If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me" (Ps 66:18).

* Return to yourself; be a judge for yourself within. Look at your hidden chamber, in the depths of the heart, there where you and God who sees are alone together, and do not take pleasure in iniquity, and God will take pleasure in you... "But verily God hath heard me" (Ps 66:19), because I do not regard iniquity in my heart, "he hath attended to the voice of my prayer" (Ps 66:19). "Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me" (Ps 66:20).

St. Augustine "This hath been by your means" [9], meaning that God wishes to hear the prayers of His priests on behalf of their people, but because of their iniquity He does not hear them until they return to Him.

10 Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought. I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. 11 For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts.
Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought.
I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. [10]

With complete frankness the Lord, the God of hosts, declares: "I have no pleasure in you," showing that with the love with which He loved them He loves all mankind. And in the clearness of day He shines with His sun upon all the nations that offer fragrant incense to the glory of His holy name.

The priests thought that they were opening the doors of the temple and kindling the altar, but since they behaved as hirelings seeking material gain for themselves, the divine voice came to them: "I have no pleasure in you." He who loves them, assuring them: "I have loved you" [2], tells them that He has no pleasure in them. It is deeply regrettable! God no longer has pleasure in the service of these priests who practice worship only for the sake of pay; whether they shut the door or kindle a fire or do any work, they demand pay! As it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his shameful gain" (Isa 56:11).
God has allowed those who serve at the altar to eat from the altar, and those who serve the Gospel to eat from the Gospel (1 Cor 9:7-14), but they do not work with a view to pay and shameful gain.
God calls us to review our depths so that we may touch the hidden motive of our worship of Him, our service and our preaching.
* Malachi, the last of all the prophets, speaks with all frankness about the rejection of Israel and the calling of the Gentiles.

St. Jerome * The Jews returned from Babylon, repaired the city, rebuilt the temple, and offered sacrifices. But before everything the prophet Malachi prophesied of the present desolation that was to come and of the abomination of the Jewish sacrifices.
* Do you not see how he stops the Jewish ways and abolishes them, and spreads the way of life of the Church and proclaims its worship?
St. John Chrysostom * You, O Jew, have not come to a pure sacrifice; I will prove to you that it is not pure.

* Why do you try, O Jews, to twist these prophetic words to another meaning as your heart dictates? You oppose the Son of God against your own salvation... For the house of Jacob or Israel is the very same people who were called and who were cast out; it was not called with respect to some and cast out with respect to others, but the whole house is called to walk in the light of the Lord... The reason for casting out the house is that its people did not walk in the light of the Lord.

St. Augustine * If a man is a Scythian or a Persian, if he has the knowledge of God and the knowledge of His Christ, and keeps the ordinances of eternal righteousness, he is circumcised with the good and profitable circumcision, and he is a friend of God, and God rejoices in his gifts and offerings...

St. Justin Martyr For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts. [11]
In the Old Testament the hymn was: "In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel" (Ps 76:1). Now all the nations glorify Him, from the rising of the sun to its going down.

* Now I return to Malachi. This man prophesied about the Church, which spread by the power of Christ and widened greatly, and he spoke to the Jews on God's lips: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts" (Mal 1:10-11). Now if we see that in this our time, in every place from the rising of the sun to its going down, this sacrifice is offered according to the order of Melchizedek, and if the Jews cannot in any circumstances deny that their sacrifices are rejected... how can they await the coming of another Christ? They read the prophecy, and see its fulfillment before their eyes. Why can they not verify that the One who fulfills this is the Christ, since no other can do it?

St. Augustine * He speaks of these Gentiles, that is, of us, who offer sacrifices to Him in every place, that is, the bread of the Eucharist and also the cup of the Eucharist, each affirming that we glorify His name while you defile it.

* God announced beforehand all the sacrifices that we offer in His name, which Jesus Christ commanded us to offer, that is, the Eucharist of the bread and the cup, which Christians offer in every place in the world, bearing witness that they are pleasing to Him. But He utterly rejects what you offer and what your priests offer.

St. Justin Martyr * The Creator of all things, his Counselor, asked his only-begotten Son to come down from heaven and turn the holy faith in God to the Gentiles, that is, to those who were ignorant of God, and to teach them the righteousness which the treacherous people had cast away from them. He had long before threatened them that He would do this, as Malachi shows.

Lactantius * These words indicate in a clear way that the former people [the Jews] cease the offerings to God, but in every place a pure sacrifice is offered to Him, and His name is glorified among the Gentiles.

St. Irenaeus * In place of the bloody sacrifice He appoints a mystical, rational, bloodless sacrifice, that of His Body and Blood, which is carried out to represent the death of the Lord... In place of the divine service limited to one place, He commands and appoints that His authority be glorified from the east to the west in every place (Ps 13:3; Mal 1:11). By this He did not abolish the Law but abolished the restrictions.

The Didascalia * When Abraham returned from the defeat of his enemies, Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, met him with bread and wine. That table had already prefigured this mystical table. And that priest was a type and image of Christ, the true Great High Priest, for the prophet says: "Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek" (Ps 110:4). And the loaves of the offering, which were an image of this bread, are therefore the pure, that is, bloodless sacrifice of which the Lord spoke by the prophet's tongue: it is offered to Him from the rising of the sun to its going down (Mal 1:11).

Father John of Damascus * Now concerning the place, let it be known that every place is suitable for prayer if a man prays well! For the Lord says: "In every place incense shall be offered unto my name" (Mal 1:11), and "I will therefore that men pray every where" (1 Tim 2:8). But let each one, if I may put it so, have if possible a chosen holy place in his house to perform his prayers in quiet without distraction.

Origen * Surely the Lord gives authority to pray in every place, in the words: "Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father" (Jn 4:21). And the words of the Apostle are lawful (2 Tim 2:8). For the word "every" does not include places set apart for human use or for defiled, disgraceful works, but it removes the limits of Jerusalem to other places in the world set apart as is fitting (for worship), in harmony with the prophecy about the sacrifice (Mal 1:11).
They are consecrated to God for the celebration of the glorious mystery.

St. Basil the Great * Since circumcision and uncircumcision belong to the one God, both have been made void in Christ because of the priority given to faith. This is the faith of which it is written that in His name shall the Gentiles trust (Isa 42:4; Mt 12:21).
Tertullian * When the only-begotten Son came, His name became wonderful in every place... Another writer says: The whole world is filled with the knowledge of the Lord (Isa 11:9).

* When do you think this happened, O Jews? When was incense offered to God in every place? When was a pure offering offered? You cannot point to any other time except after the coming of Christ. Suppose Malachi did not speak of our age, suppose he did not speak of our sacrifice but of the Jewish sacrifice, then his prophecy would be contrary to the Law. For Moses forbade the Jews to offer their sacrifice in any place other than the one the Lord God chose, for he limited their sacrifices to one appointed place. So if Malachi said that sacrifices are offered in every place, and that it should be a pure sacrifice, he contradicts and opposes what Moses said.

St. John Chrysostom * He speaks of these Gentiles, that is, of us, who in every place offer sacrifices to Him, that is, the bread of the Eucharist and also the cup of the Eucharist, affirming that we glorify His name, which you (the Jews) defile.

St. Justin Martyr * The prophet Malachi, one of the Twelve, foretold: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen" (Mal 1:10-11). These words indicate in a clear way that the old people (the Jews) will cease to offer offerings to God, but that in every place a pure sacrifice will be offered to Him, and that His name will be glorified among the Gentiles. But what other name is glorified among the Gentiles like that of our Lord, by which the Father and also man are glorified? And because this is the name of His Son, who became flesh by Him, He calls it "his name."

St. Irenaeus * It is now the time when the true worshippers worship the Father neither in Jerusalem nor on Mount Gerizim but in spirit and in truth (Jn 4:20-23). Therefore God dwells in the heart. If you are looking for the place of God, the pure heart is His place, for He says by the prophet: "I will dwell in them, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, saith the Lord" (2 Cor 6:16; Lev 26:12).

Origen * It has now been proved from the Holy Scriptures that the Jews lost the inheritance because they rejected Christ, and we who are from the Gentiles have taken their place. Jeremiah says: "I have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage; I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies. Mine heritage is unto me as a lion in the forest; it crieth out against me: therefore have I hated it" (Jer 12:7-8). And also Malachi: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles" (Mal 1:10-11). Isaiah also says: "It shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory" (Isa 66:18).

And he himself says in another place, in the person of the Father to the Son: "I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles; To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house" (Isa 42:6-7).
Lactantius * On the Lord's day, gather together to break bread and give thanks, but first confess your sins, that your sacrifice may be pure.
In any case, whoever has a dispute with his brother, let him not take part in your gathering until he is reconciled, so that your sacrifice may not be defiled.
For this is what the Lord said: "In every place and at every time offer to My name a pure offering, for I am a great King, saith the Lord, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles" (Mal 1:11).
The Didache

12 But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the LORD is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible. 13 Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD. 14 But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.
But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the LORD is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible. [12]

He renews the grave accusation that He had already directed at them in verse 7. Since they violated the divine holy things and the worship, it is no wonder that God drives them away from before Him. They said, not with their mouths but by their conduct, that the table of the Lord is polluted, for they did not lead the people to honor the altar and to offer the finest they had to God, so they became preachers of contempt for the temple of the Lord and His altar.
Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it!
And ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering.
Should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD. [13]

The second accusation directed at the priests is that they thought their task heavy and very burdensome, so they fulfilled it in a spirit of grumbling. For this reason the Lord reproaches His people in Micah: "wherein have I wearied thee?" (Mic 6:3), and in Isaiah He says: "I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense. Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with money, neither hast thou filled me with the fat of thy sacrifices" (Isa 43:23-24).
God does not seek the offering but the one who offers the offering. "My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways" (Prov 26:23).

Unclean worship turns from the sense of delight and sweetness in fellowship with God into hardship, weariness and boredom, in which man grumbles and is puffed up by his worship instead of enjoying humility. In this way man feels weariness and boredom even in his communal or personal prayers, or his fasting, or his giving, in one form or another.
But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing.
For I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen. [14]

They offer defective sacrifices, not because suitable sacrifices are lacking, but out of contempt and disdain for the worship of God. They have the best flocks, and what is fit for the service and honor of God, yet they offered the worst they had. They try craftily to present human justifications for offering defective sacrifices. Thus they claim to honor God while they are offending Him.
By their craftiness they fell under the curse instead of enjoying the heavenly blessings, for He says of them: "cursed be the deceiver."

He rebukes His priests and His people because they behaved in a way that the pagans did not, for His name is great and dreadful among the Gentiles, while the Jews and their priests made light of His name, His temple and His sacrifices. As the psalmist says: "O clap your hands, all ye people... For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth" (Ps 47:1-2).
* It is not enough for Him that one nation be subject to Him; He paid a great price that came out of His side in order to buy the whole world.
St. Augustine
Sanctify me, that I may offer You a holy sacrifice!
* Your voice resounds in the depths of my heart:
I have loved you, and chosen you as My son.
I redeemed you with My blood that you may enjoy fellowship in My glories!
* You chose me before You created me, You knew me before I existed, You prepared glory for me when I was still nothing.
What shall I render to You, who anticipate me with Your love?
* Take away from me all pride and hypocrisy, for I shall not be justified before You.
I have sinned, for I did not honor You as a Father, nor fear You as my Master.
Kindle my heart with the fire of Your love, and nail Your fear within me.
* In my folly I despised Your name, and offered unclean sacrifices, for I did not offer You the firstfruits of my time, nor give priority to meeting with You.
I was busy with temporal things as though they were eternal, and ignored my eternity as though it were an illusion and a fantasy.
I have wronged Your long-suffering, O You who await my return to You.
* I have sinned, for I was often occupied with formalities, and counted worship of You a heavy duty.
Shine upon my heart that it may cleave to You.
And let Your Holy Spirit work in me, that I may walk always in the Spirit.
* Often I came to You as a lame man, limping between two ways.
Carry me to You and in You, O true Way.
Take away all sickness from my soul, O heavenly Physician.
Lift up my face to You, and let me count all things as refuse for Your sake!
* Shine upon me, O Sun of Righteousness, as upon my brethren, that the whole world may be enlightened by Your light.
And let all offer pure incense to Your name.
And let all enjoy the sacrifice of Your Body and Blood, which were given, and let Your name be glorified in every man!
* Turn the whole world into a holy place for You, and let all enjoy fellowship with You, and let all offer a pure, holy sacrifice, as all cleave to the sacrifice of Your Cross.
And reign, O heavenly King, over all mankind.

1 And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. 2 If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart. 3 Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it. 4 And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the LORD of hosts.
And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. [1]

Perhaps the priests justify their faults mentioned in the previous chapter by saying that the unclean and defective offerings and sacrifices which they present on the altar are not their fault, but the fault of the people who refuse to give God the best they have. So this chapter comes to uncover what is in the hearts of the priests themselves. The commandment directed here to the priests does not concern offerings and sacrifices but the hearts of the priests, their intentions, their life and their conduct. If the work of the priest is to intercede for the people by offering sacrifices as a type of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ, then it befits the priest to be sanctified. If the priest is not pure, how can his heart cry out for the purity and sanctification of the hearts of others?
If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you.
And I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart. [2]

God, the Searcher of hearts, knows perfectly that their practice of the priestly work was not for the sake of God's glory; the fault is in the heart itself, therefore the curse comes upon them instead of blessings.

Since they do not give their hearts to the Lord, but for the sake of temporal glory or material greed, the curse comes upon them, so that they lose their honor, even the temporal, and their blessings, even the material. They lose what is heavenly, and also what is earthly.

* It is a heavy burden that priests are bound to defend the glory of God and work for it, so that we may not appear to neglect any such thing, when God urges us and says: "And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings" (cf. Mal 2:1-4).

St. Cyprian * When the shepherd walks on steep and rugged places, the flock follows him and falls into the pit of destruction. Hence the Lord grieves over the evil knowledge of the shepherds, and says by the prophet: "Seemeth it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures? and to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet? And as for my flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet" (Ezek 34:18-19).

It is clear that when the shepherds drink from clear and pure waters, they are refreshed from the spring of truth by their right understanding, but they corrupt the holy contemplation by their evil life when they foul the waters with their feet. It is self-evident that the flock will drink of these polluted waters fouled by these feet, and then refrain from carrying out the teachings it has heard, because it imitates the evil example it sees. The flock longs to do the good that the shepherds say, but it is turned aside by the evil they do, and so it absorbs the mud along with what it drinks, since it draws from a polluted spring.

For this reason the prophet wrote saying that the wicked priests have become a snare for the destruction of the people: "Hear ye this, O priests... for judgment is toward you, because ye have been a snare" (Hos 5:1), "the prophet is a snare of a fowler" (Hos 9:8), and the Lord also says by the prophet concerning the shepherds: "and caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity" (Ezek 44:12).
No one does more harm to the Church than those who have the appearance of holiness and its title but behave corruptly.
Father Gregory (the Great)

* This is your duty, O bishop: not to ignore the faults of the people nor to make light of the repentant, lest you destroy the Lord's flock through lack of skill, or insult His new name sealed upon His people, and you yourself be rebuked just as the ancient shepherds were rebuked, when God spoke of them through Jeremiah: [Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have defiled my portion] (cf. Jer 12:10).
The Apostolic Constitutions Since priests fall under the curse, they in turn become a cause of cursing for those among the people who walk with them in the same way.

* Let the people not deceive themselves, thinking that they are safe from the contagion of sin while they cleave to a sinful priest and render obedience to their unjust leader, illegitimate in his episcopate. They are blamed by the prophet Hosea: "their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted" (Hos 9:4). This teaching shows clearly that all share together in the sin of the corruption of the sacrifice of the blasphemous, unjust priest.
St. Cyprian the Martyr Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it. [3]

The aim of the priestly work is to create the joyful heavenly atmosphere among the people, but because of the corruption of their hearts and intentions their life was turned into a cause of bitterness, famine and sorrow among the people.

When the spiritual leaders turn aside from holiness, the blessing flees and the curse comes. Just as the earth was cursed because of the sin of our first parents Adam and Eve, so that it brought forth thorns and thistles, the prophet Isaiah says: "Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength, therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants... but the harvest shall flee away in the day of the destroying blow and hopeless sorrow" (Isa 17:10-11). And the prophet Hosea says: "For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up" (Hos 8:7). And the prophet Jeremiah: "They have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns" (Jer 12:13).
* You reap no fruit from the service of idols, for their sheaves are like ears of wheat scattered by the wind; from the outside they appear to be full of grain, but inside they have no yield.
* He says: when you forget the Maker of the good things with you, you sow unfaithfulness and reap ingratitude. Well then, you will reap the fruits of your plantings and your seed.

Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus The text in the Catholic edition reads: "Behold, I will cut off your arms, and scatter dung upon your faces, the dung of your feasts, and it shall carry you away with it." So instead of the honor, glory and blessing that the priests enjoy as servants of God working for the edification of His people, they become men with their arms cut off, dung is thrown on their faces, and they lose the joy of the feasts.

Perhaps he means by the dung here what is in the entrails of the sacrifices when they are washed, for since they offer defective sacrifices with corrupt hearts, instead of receiving portions of the sacrifice to eat as priests of God, God throws its dung on their faces as a sign of the shame that comes upon them, making them despised among the people and base. This is the lot of the servant who seeks not the glory of God but his own glory and his own material gain. They become like a dunghill, fit only to have dung thrown on them.
And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. [4]

God affirms that what Malachi speaks is not from himself, but is the word of God which He sent to them for their repentance, sending it to them because of His covenant with Levi, that he be sanctified for the sake of the divine service.

In all generations the Lord wishes to establish with His children and His people an everlasting covenant, that they may enjoy the heavenly inheritance. As the psalmist says: "He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations" (Ps 105:8).

* After saying "He hath remembered his covenant for ever," which we must understand as a covenant that remains forever, the covenant of justification and eternal inheritance, which God promises through faith, he added: "the word which he commanded to a thousand generations." What does he mean by the word "commanded"? The commandment here is faith, by which the just shall live (Rom 1:17), and the eternal inheritance is set over against this faith.

St. Augustine * "They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law; and forgat his works, and his wonders that he had shewed them" (Ps 78:9-10). They rebelled against Him who renewed them in Baptism... He divided the sea and caused them to pass through it, and made the waters stand as in a vessel. And He led them with a cloud in the daytime (Ps 78:12-14).
* "My mercy will I keep for him for evermore, and my covenant shall stand fast with him" (Ps 89:28). He keeps His mercy continually in the Church, which He saves by the covenant of His commandments.
* The Law was merely the beginning of the covenant, and the Gospel is its completion.
St. Jerome

5 My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name. 6 The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. 7 For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.

When God established His covenant with the sons of Levi, especially with Aaron and his sons, He did not lay a heavy yoke upon them. He offered a covenant "of life and peace." God set them apart to be a cause of life for His people, and of peace for them, through their holy service.

If God made a covenant with His people, He made it in particular with the tribe of Levi. "For the LORD had spoken unto Moses, saying, Only thou shalt not number the tribe of Levi, neither take the sum of them among the children of Israel: But thou shalt appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of testimony... they shall bear the tabernacle, and all the vessels thereof, and they shall minister unto it, and shall encamp round about the tabernacle" (Num 3:12). As He also said to him: "And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office" (Ex 28:1), as it is said: "Aaron the saint of the LORD" (Ps 106:16).
God opens the doors of heaven to pour out upon the soul that fears the Lord and bears His fear within. He grants us eternal life and inner peace if we fear Him.
My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me.
And was afraid before my name. [5]

The priest is entrusted with the divine covenant that he may be the messenger of the LORD of hosts, the messenger of the covenant of life and peace. When Moses blessed the tribes before his departure he said of Levi: "Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant" (Deut 33:9). So it befitted Levi, as a servant of the Holy One, to concentrate all his energies on the divine commandment and the divine covenant above every relationship, until he seemed as one who does not see his father and mother, does not acknowledge his brethren, and does not know his children.
What does He mean by saying: "My covenant was with him of life and peace"?

If eternal death has come upon man because of sin, and he has lost his inner peace and his peace with God and with his brethren, because he turned his back to God, the giver of peace, then the aim of the divine covenant is to raise the spiritually dead to enjoy Christ "the Resurrection," so that man lives and does not die, and reconciliation takes place between him and God, so that he is filled with peace within himself as well as with his brethren. This is the work of the priest, with which he ought to be occupied and from which he ought not to turn aside.

* He saved mankind, the work of His hands, and not any other work; that is, what He created for Himself He saved for Himself. He created man who perished through his evil. He (the Lord Christ) died in order to keep man for Himself by His right hand.

* He is the Lord who says: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready." I am ready here, and I am ready in the life to come. I am a Savior on earth, I am a Savior in heaven. I give eternal life to angels and men together.
St. Jerome The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips.
He walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. [6]
It befits the priest to have knowledge of heavenly things, to live them and bear witness to them before the people, so that he brings forth out of his treasure things new and old (Mt 13:52).
For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts. [7]

Solomon the Wise sees that the priest must be wise, so that his lips overflow with words of knowledge and wisdom, by which he draws many to the way of truth, for he says: "In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found... The lips of the righteous guide many" (Prov 10:13-21).

Nothing occupies the priest's heart but the Law, or the divine commandment, and his lips utter nothing but what accords with the Law: "they should seek the law at his mouth." All that he utters is ascribed to the One who commissioned him, who sent him, "for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" [7].

It befits the priest to realize his position as the messenger of the LORD of hosts, having a true, heavenly, divine vision. As the Lord said to the prophet Isaiah: "Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he seeth" (Isa 21:6). It befits the priest to cry out to God, saying: "My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights" (Isa 21:8). Thus the priest stands night and day, knowing no rest for his body, looking continually upon his people as with the eyes of the Lord, in the midst of their joys as by day and all the nights in the midst of their afflictions. He cares for them while the Sun of Righteousness shines upon them, as he cares for their salvation when the darkness of night comes upon them because of their turning away from the Sun of Righteousness.

Moreover it befits the believer, for his part, while seeking the counsel of the LORD of hosts, to resort to prayer and supplication, together with asking "the messenger of the LORD of hosts," and not to cease seeking knowledge and the divine will.

* The work of a messenger is this, to pass on from one to another what he has been told. For this reason the priest too is called a messenger (Mal 2:7), because he does not speak his own words, but the words of him who sends him.

St. John Chrysostom * We must fear lest the prophet's violent rebuke be directed at us: "dumb dogs, they cannot bark" (Isa 56:10). By the barking of dogs and the shepherd's staff the ferocity of wolves is resisted. Now surely priests are not ordained to be stewards of fields or sowers of lands, but to be tillers of souls, which the Apostle surely speaks of when he said: "I have planted, Apollos watered." And again he said: "For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry" (1 Cor 3:9). These truths must be received with great fear by all priests, who cannot be ignorant of the divine law and the canonical regulations, as the Apostle says: [If anyone belongs to the Lord, let him know what I say; but if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant] (cf. 1 Cor 14:37-38). For this reason, let him fear completely what the Lord said by the prophet: "Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge" (Isa 5:13). Besides this: "He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination" (Prov 28:9). "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge" (Mal 2:7). It is written concerning the priests' garments that when they enter the temple there must be golden bells on the hems of the garments. What are these but that when all the priests of the Lord enter the Church they do not cease to cry out, that is, to preach about the last things, the end of the world and the coming judgment? By their continual proclamation of the rewards of the righteous and the punishments of the wicked, they urge the good to what is better, and turn the wicked from their sinful conduct through fear of the coming judgment.

Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles * Nothing holy was formerly offered or practiced in the temple without the priest. For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth, "for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts," as the prophet says (Mal 2:7).

The Didascalia * It was said to sinners: "Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee: and they have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity" (Lam 2:14). It is to be noted that teachers were sometimes called "prophets" in the Holy Scripture, because they showed the nature of the present and announced the future. It is as though God accuses them of lying if they praise the doers of evil and acquit them instead of condemning their faults, and that out of fear of them.

If shepherds avoid using words of rebuke, they fail to disclose the faults of the wicked. For words of rebuke are truly the key that reveals the sin which the one who commits it often does not feel. For this reason the Apostle Paul says: "Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers" (Titus 1:9), and Malachi also says: "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" (Mal 2:7). Therefore the Lord warns on the lips of Isaiah, saying: "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet" (Isa 58:1). He who enters the priesthood takes the office of a messenger who cries with a loud voice, and goes before the coming of the just Judge, who follows him with a terrible appearance.
Father Gregory (the Great)

entries.section: 3. Their corrupting the covenant with God:

paragraphs.text: 8 But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. 9 Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.
Ye have caused many to stumble at the law.
Ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. [8]

"Ye have caused many to stumble at the law" [8], either by their interpreting the Law in a literal, killing way, so that it became a burden on the soul, or by applying it as they please for the sake of their personal interests, flattering the rich and being harsh on the poor and the weak. These turn even the Gospel of Christ, which is a savor of life unto life, into "a savour of death unto death" (2 Cor 2:16), and the Lord Christ Himself becomes to them a "rock of offence" (Rom 9:33).

It is a cause of stumbling for the people that the priest turn aside from the way, and betray the covenant that God established with Levi. What is turning aside from the divine way but the priest's being occupied with something other than the salvation of his own soul and the salvation of his children or the people? This is the way of the Lord, who wants all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of God. Thus they corrupt the covenant with God the Lover of mankind.

* The just Judge disowns them and ignores them, for those whose trials and sufferings He eases in this world are in truth rejected by Him. Therefore the Lord of glory says to such as these, even if they perform miracles: "I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity" (Lk 13:27; Mt 7:23). The voice of divine truth rebukes the folly of such shepherds, saying: "they are shepherds that cannot understand" (Isa 56:11). Again the Lord reproves them, saying: "they that handle the law knew me not" (Jer 2:8). And therefore divine truth complains of these shepherds because they did not know Him. For no one understands the loftiness of the service of leadership except those who know Him, but those who are ignorant of what belongs to the Lord, the Lord ignores them, as the Apostle Paul says: "But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant" (1 Cor 14:38).

* The unworthiness of the shepherd is often joined with the unworthiness of the flock, so if the shepherds do not possess the light of knowledge as a result of their personal sin, the flock accordingly stumbles because of its ignorance, according to the punishment of judgment. For this reason the Lord of glory Jesus said: "And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch" (Mt 15:14; Lk 6:39). In this the psalmist said prophetically: "Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake" (Ps 69:23). The leaders are in truth eyes, for they are at the front of the highest ranks and have undertaken to make the way plain, while those who follow them are bound to them and are therefore called "loins." Thus when the eyes are darkened the loins also are bent, for when the leaders lose the light of knowledge, those who follow them bow down under the yoke of their sins.
Father Gregory (the Great)

* So the priestly ministry is a trade. Therefore the prophet says to the children of Israel: [Your tavern-keepers mix water with their wine] (cf. Isa 1:22) LXX. St. Isaiah is not speaking of tavern-keepers who in their turn, in their service of the taverns, adulterate pure wine with water. It is difficult to think that this blessed man is speaking of this matter as if he were a civil judge concerned that people dilute strong drink with water. Rather he speaks of tavern-keepers who dwell not in taverns but in churches. These do not offer the thirsty a cup of passions but of virtue. They do not serve the cup of strong drink but the cup of the Savior. He rebukes these tavern-keepers and criticizes them, complaining that they mix the wine with water. This is what he criticizes in them: that though they were appointed for the divine works, they became occupied with human affairs, as the prophet himself says: "Every one is busy with his own house." For if a priest neglects the priestly work and is immersed in worldly pleasures, he mixes the wine with water, that is, he mixes warm things with trivial, cold things.

Father Maximus, bishop of Turin It is dangerous for the shepherd to lose the spirit of discernment, so that the word meant for enlightenment turns into a stumbling block for the people, as the Lord Christ said: "They be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch" (Mt 15:14). And the prophet Isaiah says: "We grope for the wall like the blind, and as they that have no eyes we feel our way; we have stumbled at noonday as in darkness, in the mist as dead men" (Isa 59:9-10).

* They read the Holy Scripture, and do not see the truth in it, and they resemble the blind who walk feeling the wall without seeing. And they fall at noon as at midnight. You see what misery this is for all. Although the Sun of Righteousness shines on the whole world, they (the Jews) stumble and fall as in the death of night. They sigh like a dead person. They spend life in great sorrow so that their existence seems like death.

Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * They are blind leaders of a blind people. Who are these blind leaders? The Pharisees, whose minds the god of this age blinded, because they do not believe, since they did not believe in Jesus Christ. The god of this age has blinded them so that the light of the gospel of the glory of God in the face of Christ should not shine on them (2 Cor 4:4). We must avoid being led by these blind persons. It befits us not only to do this but also to listen carefully to those who are engaged in leadership in the way of sound teaching, and to apply with right judgment what they say. Let us do this so that we ourselves may not appear blind, because we do not see the meaning of the Holy Scriptures.

entries.section: 3. Their corrupting the covenant with God:

paragraphs.text: Origen Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law. [9]

Since the people perceive in the priests that instead of being a source of divine blessing, they have come to bear the curse [2], therefore the Lord says: "Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people" [9].

Besides turning aside from the divine way and corrupting the covenant, they are partial in the law. They choose from it what they please, and ignore what does not accord with their evil will. They fulfill the outward appearances, and do not care about inner purity. They do not respect all His commandments. The psalmist says: "Then shall I not be ashamed, when I have respect unto all thy commandments" (Ps 119:6).

Perhaps by partiality in the law he means their using the commandment in partiality toward persons, flattering some and being harsh to others, not with wisdom for their salvation but to achieve personal interests, whereas "there is no respect of persons with God" (Rom 2:11). As Elihu says: "How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands" (Job 34:19).

entries.section: 4. Corrupting the covenant with one's neighbor:

paragraphs.text: Have we not all one father?
Hath not one God created us?
Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers? [10]

They ignored their brethren as sons of one heavenly Father and creatures made by one God, so each of them dealt treacherously with his brother. Since they do not love God they do not love their brethren, and also by dealing treacherously with one another they insult the Father of all and the Creator of all. The Apostle Paul says: "One God and Father of all" (Eph 4:6), and the prophet Isaiah says: "But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand" (Isa 64:8).

* There (in heaven) there is no love with special regard for a neighbor, but all will love one another abundantly in one pattern. There they neither marry wives nor beget children, and there is no distinction between male and female, but all will be sons of their Father who is in heaven, as the prophet said: "Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?" (Mal 2:10).

* As for what I said, that there will be no wives and no distinction between male and female, our Lord and His apostles taught this.
